sights.description: A Shingon temple called Shinano Koya, once ancestral temple of Azumi and Chikuma people, and famous for azaleas.

stays.description: Lodging in Kamiyamada Onsen, Chikuma, with free-flowing hot-spring rooms, private dining, and an open-air bath overlooking the Chikuma River.

stays.name_en: Togura Kamiyamada Onsen Yumoto Kamiyamada Hotel
stays.name_ja: 戸倉上山田温泉 湯元 上山田ホテル

stays.description: Inn in Kamiyamada Onsen, Chikuma, with a free-flowing indoor hot spring bath open 24 hours.

stays.name: Hotel Enzanso
stays.name_ja: ホテル圓山荘
stays.description: Hotel in Kamiyamada Onsen, Chikuma, with two free-flowing natural hot spring sources and an open-air bath.

stays.name_ja: 梅むら旅館 うぐいす亭
stays.description: Ryokan in Kamiyamada Onsen, Chikuma.

stays.name: Shunjuan Kikusui
stays.name_ja: 旬樹庵菊水
stays.description: Inn in Kamiyamada Onsen, Chikuma, with 16 rooms, an open-air hot spring bath, and a private bath.

stays.name: Kamiyamada Onsen Yuzan
stays.name_ja: 上山田温泉 湯楽 ゆうざん
stays.description: Accommodation in Kamiyamada Onsen, Chikuma, with karaoke, table tennis, sister-property baths, and a 103-square-meter room.

stays.name: Kamesei Ryokan
stays.name_ja: 亀清旅館
stays.description: Ryokan in Kamiyamada Onsen, Chikuma, with a hot spring, a detached-style 10-tatami room, and courtyard gardens.

stays.name: Shunjuan Wakanoyu
stays.name_ja: 旬樹庵 若の湯
stays.description: Inn in Kamiyamada Onsen, Chikuma, with a hot spring, sister-property bath access, and a Japanese room with a veranda.

stays.name: Business Hotel Green Plaza
stays.name_ja: 姉妹館の天然温泉に入れるビジネスホテルグリーンプラザ
stays.description: Business hotel in Kamiyamada Onsen, Chikuma, with free parking, all-smoking rooms, and sister-property hot spring access.

stays.name: Hotel Platon
stays.name_ja: 天然温泉 朝食付き ホテルプラトン
stays.description: Hotel in Kamiyamada Onsen, Chikuma, with night hot spring access, breakfast, free parking, and in-room smoking.

stays.name: Togura Kamiyamada Onsen Yunoyado Fukujuso
stays.name_ja: 戸倉上山田温泉 湯の宿 福寿草
stays.description: Onsen inn with a free-flowing hot spring bath and Japanese-style rooms in Isobe, Chikuma.

stays.name: Ryotei Takano
stays.name_ja: 全5室源泉かけ流し露天風呂付 個室食の宿 旅亭たかの
stays.description: Inn in Kamiyamada Onsen, Chikuma, with five rooms with free-flowing open-air baths and private kaiseki dining.

day_to_day.name: Kinkei no Yu, Kanazawa Hot Spring
day_to_day.description: Large and small rest rooms provide a casual space for refreshment and health.

day_to_day.name: Shiotsubo no Yu, Yonezawa Hot Spring
day_to_day.description: The barrier-free facility offers alternating baths and well-equipped dry and mist saunas.

activities.name: Sogyo Taisho Jugo Nen Tateshina Oya Yu Onsen
activities.description: Hot spring in Chino.

activities.name: YATSU Trek Club
activities.description: Chino-based guides offer Yatsugatake hiking, winter mountaineering, and snowshoeing, with advice for beginners.

activities.name: Lake Shirakaba Royal Hill Ski Resort
activities.description: An 80 percent clear-sky rate and snowmaking keep this compact resort stable for all levels.

activities.name: Pilatus Tateshina Snow Resort
activities.description: Seven courses from 2,237 meters offer premium snow and rime ice, with one ropeway and two lifts.

activities.name: Ikenotaira Snow Park
activities.description: Shirakaba Resort pairs slopes and a hotel, with snow play, an indoor pool, hot springs, and lessons from four.

activities.name: Tateshina Hot Springs
activities.description: Famous as Takeda Shingen's hidden hot spring, with lakes and golf courses nearby.

food.name: Peter's Field
food.description: Kitchen car mainly at Tateshina lakeside selling light meals and sweets; the menu changes by season and may use garden-grown wild strawberries, raspberries and grapes. Closed irregularly.

food.name: Flora & Fauna
food.name_ja: 八ヶ岳カフェ＆ベーカリー Flora & Fauna
food.description: Cafe and bakery on the Venus Line serving house-made bread, seasonal pasta, coffee and Otari maple-sap tea; open 11:00-15:00 (last order 14:30), closed Wed-Fri in summer and Mon-Fri in winter.

food.name: Yatsugatake Octet
food.description: Cafe and bakery in the Chino Station area serving Tateshina beef loco moco with a hamburger steak, runny fried egg and vegetables; open 10:00-19:00; closed Thursdays and certain days.

food.name: Tateshina Gouter
food.description: Cafe serving a lunch-only beef stew with salad, bread and a drink, plus cake and drinks; cakes and Jomon cookies are also sold. Open 11:00-18:00, closed Wednesday and Thursday.

food.name: Shokudo Cafe Field Note
food.name_ja: 食堂カフェ フィールドノート
food.description: Cafe serving coffee and handmade dishes; 890-yen lunch includes soup, salad and coffee (not Sundays or holidays), evening a la carte includes bakery gratin (880 yen), open 11:30-15:00 and 17:00-23:00, closed Tuesdays.

food.name: Tateshina Jiyu Noen 808 Cafe
food.description: Farm-shop cafe serving a highland-vegetable salad and bakery goods made with Tateshina and Yatsugatake ingredients; open 10:00-17:30, closed Wednesdays.

food.name: TOP'S360°
food.description: Cafe-restaurant at the Skyliner lift terminus in Kurumayama Skypark serving oven pizza, taco rice, venison keema curry, desserts and drinks; summer 9:00-16:00, winter meals 11:00-14:00 and cafe 9:00-15:45.

food.name: Coffee & Beans Kariomon
food.description: Lakeside cafe at Lake Shirakaba serving freshly roasted coffee; roasting experiences and coffee classes are offered; open 10:00-17:00; closed Mondays (Tuesdays when Monday is a holiday).

food.name: Cafe Rest Mokuba
food.description: Cafe-restaurant beside Pilatus Ski Resort with glass walls facing the slopes; open in winter only, 10:00-16:00, irregular closures.

food.name: Tateshina Kogen Barakura English Garden
food.name_ja: 蓼科高原 バラクラ イングリッシュ ガーデン
food.description: Garden venue serving afternoon tea, handmade scones and cakes, and British country lunch; open every day, with hours that vary by season.

food.name: Utsuwa to Cafe Tosenbo Suguridaira
food.name_ja: 器とCafe 陶仙房 須栗平
food.description: Gallery cafe in a renovated early-Showa farmhouse in Chino, showing local artists' crafts and serving local seasonal ingredients; hours and closed days change by season.

food.name: Merry Cafe Snowy
food.description: Forest cafe in Chino serving house-roasted coffee and homemade lunch; dogs allowed inside and on the terrace, with a dog run. Tue-Wed 11:30-14:00, Thu-Sat 11:30-17:00 (LO 16:00); closed Sun-Mon; hours vary by season.

food.name: Mori no Kitchen queue
food.description: Highland cafe in Tateshina, Chino, serving French bread and a chef's handmade menu, plus coffee brewed with Tateshina water; open mid-April to November, 10:00-17:00, closed Thursdays.

food.name: Suiyō
food.description: Chinese or Asian restaurant in Chino.

food.name: Mela Nataraj
food.name_ja: インド料理 メラ・ナタラジ
food.description: Indian restaurant in front of Lake Tateshina serving curries with seasonal vegetables from its own farm and natural-yeast naan; a mild children's set is available; open 11:00-22:00 (last order 21:30).

food.name: Restaurant Ryujin-tei
food.name_ja: レストラン 竜神亭

food.name: Le Jardin
food.name_ja: HÔTEL de L'ALPAGE内メインダイニング【 Le Jardin】
food.description: French restaurant in Hôtel de l'Alpage using local ingredients, with more than 2,000 wines imported from France; lunch 11:30-15:00, cafe/bar 11:30-22:00, dinner 17:00-22:00; closed Tue-Wed except peak periods.

food.name: Tateshina Kohan Apron Mark
food.name_ja: たてしな湖畔 エプロンマーク
food.description: Western restaurant at Lake Tateshina using Nagano ingredients; lunch 11:00-16:00 (last order 15:00), dinner 17:00-21:00 (last order 20:00), closed Wednesday and Thursday, which may vary by season.

food.name: CARPE DIEM
food.description: French countryside home-cooking restaurant in the Kurumayama pension village, open weekends and holidays only; lunch 11:30-14:00 and dinner 18:00-20:00.

food.name: Garden Kitchen Poan
food.name_ja: ガーデンキッチン歩庵
food.description: French restaurant serving kaiseki-style French cuisine with seasonal vegetables; lunch 11:30-14:00, dinner 17:30-20:00 (last order 19:30), closed Wednesday and Thursday. Reserve by the previous day.

food.name: Cafe Andante
food.description: Restaurant in Chino Civic Hall serving spaghetti, hamburg steak, lunch sets, pizza, soft drinks and desserts; open 10:00-20:00 (lunch 11:00-14:00), closed Tuesdays.

food.name: Coffee & Restaurant Woodpecker
food.name_ja: コーヒー&レストラン ウッドペッカー
food.description: Italian restaurant serving spaghetti, with private hire for about 8 to 50 people; open 11:00-22:00, closed Thursdays.

food.name: Osteria Shirakaba
food.name_ja: 高原の小さなイタリア料理店 オステリア白樺
food.description: Italian restaurant on Kurumayama Kogen serving handmade pizza and pasta; open 11:30-15:00 (last order 14:00) and 18:00-21:00 (last order 20:00), closed Wednesday and the third Tuesday (irregular in winter).

food.name: Les Cerisiers
food.description: Restaurant serving 100% buckwheat galettes with cheese or ham and Shinshu game; open 11:00-15:00 (last order 14:00), irregular closures, and Wednesday and Friday dinners require reservation 48 hours ahead.

food.name: THE Switchback TATESHiNA farm and trails
food.name_en: THE Switchback TATESHiNA farm and trails
food.name_ja: 新窯料理と山歩き THE Switchback TATESHiNA farm and trails
food.description: Wood-fired restaurant serving pizza, kiln-roasted vegetables and Tateshina beef T-bone steak; 11:30-15:00 and 17:00-22:00 (last order), closed the second Wednesday and every Thursday.

food.name: Tateshina Il Porto
food.description: Italian restaurant with its own garden, serving highland vegetables, herbs and handmade pasta; lunch 11:00-14:30 (weekends and holidays 11:30-15:00), dinner 17:00-21:00, closed Tuesdays (open daily in August).

food.name: Restaurant DisMoi
food.name_ja: レストラン ディモア
food.description: Restaurant DisMoi in Chino serves prix-fixe courses with seafood, locally raised meat and chef-grown vegetables, plus wine; lunch pasta sets are also available.

food.name: Osteria Shirakaba
food.description: Small Italian restaurant at Kurumayama Kogen on the Venus Line serving handmade pizza and pasta, including pizza formaggio (1,380 yen) and tiramisu (570 yen); lunch sets are 1,890 yen.

food.name: Sakura Saku
food.description: Horse-meat specialty izakaya offering various horse-meat dishes; lunch 11:30-14:00, dinner 17:00-22:30, closed Tuesdays.

food.name: Bar & Live the Piano Man
food.name_ja: Bar & ライブハウス ピアノマン
food.description: Bar and live house serving food and drinks; open 19:00-25:00, closed Mondays, Tuesdays and certain other days.

food.name: Shokushuya Umaimonoya Nishiki
food.name_ja: 食酒屋 うまいものや にし季
food.description: Izakaya a 3-minute walk from the station serving thick handmade tamagoyaki made with five eggs from designated domestic farms, plus basashi and shio-koji chicken karaage; open 17:00-23:00; closed Sundays.

food.name: Ainojuku
food.name_ja: おごっつぉう居酒屋 あいのじゅく
food.description: Izakaya on the first floor of Hotel Chino; soft fillet cutlet is the most popular dish. Open 17:30-22:00, closed irregularly.

food.name: Ishokuya Ao Togarashi
food.name_ja: 居食や 青とうがらし
food.description: Izakaya in an old house at the Tateshina entrance on the Venus Line, serving salads with seasonal local ingredients and pasta; open 18:00-24:00, closed Tuesdays (irregular closures December-March).

food.name: Glamorous Dining Tateshina
food.name_ja: グラマラスダイニング蓼科
food.description: Serves outdoor BBQ in a forest setting in Tateshina; open 11:00-20:00 by reservation, some lunch items available without reservation, closed Wednesdays.

food.name: Tateshina Beef Ittou
food.description: Yakiniku restaurant operated by Tateshina beef producers, serving that beef including uncommon cuts; lunch 11:00-14:30 (last order 14:00), dinner 17:00-22:00 (last order 21:00), closed Tuesdays.

food.name: Country Restaurant Takumitei
food.name_ja: カントリーレストラン 匠亭
food.description: Log-house restaurant serving venison, wild boar, seasonal mountain vegetables, mushrooms and salt-grilled iwana; open 12:00-14:00 and 17:30-20:00, closed Tuesdays.

food.name: Tajimaya Konosuke Chino-ten
food.name_ja: 但馬家 幸之助 ちの店
food.description: Yakiniku restaurant serving beef from its own Matsuki Ranch in Kobuchizawa, plus homemade kimchi, stone-grilled kalbi udon and salt ramen; open 11:30-14:00 and 17:00-22:00 daily.

food.name: Harupin Miso Ramen Raizo Chino Main Store
food.name_en: Harupin Miso Ramen Raizo Chino Main Store
food.name_ja: ハルピン 味噌らーめん 雷蔵 茅野本店

food.name: Shinshu Hon-teuchi Soba Katsuyama Soba-ten
food.name_ja: 信州本手打ちそば 勝山そば店
food.description: Handmade soba shop serving thick, dark country-style soba; nabeyaki udon is more popular than soba in winter. Lunch 11:00-14:00, dinner 17:00-19:00, closed Wednesdays.

food.name: Shinshu Teuchi Soba Kobo Yurakuan
food.name_ja: 信州手打ちそば工房 遊楽庵
food.description: Serves stone-milled 100% soba made in-house from domestic buckwheat and Yokotani Gorge spring water, with no binder; open 11:00-15:00 (last order 14:30), closed irregularly.

food.name: Teuchi Sobakiri Ryozantei
food.name_ja: 手打ち蕎麦切り 蓼山亭
food.description: Serves 100% buckwheat soba that the owner grows and mills; open from 11:00 until sold out, closed Wednesdays except during Golden Week and summer.

food.name: Shinshu Soba to Shusai Sarashina
food.name_ja: 信州蕎麦と酒菜 さらしな
food.description: Hand-cut soba shop about 5 minutes from JR Chino Station west exit, also serving evening meals with drinks; open 11:00-14:00 and 17:00-21:00, or until soba runs out; closed Mondays (Tuesday if Monday is a holiday).

food.name: Toge no Chaya Fuseian
food.description: Handmade soba shop using spring water from Mount Moriya; open 10:00-16:30 or until sold out, closed on irregular days and from December to March.

food.name: Kuretakebo
food.description: Handmade soba restaurant milling its own Shinshu buckwheat flour; open 10:30-21:00, closed Thursdays (another day if Thursday is a holiday).

food.name: Sobakiri Dogen
food.description: Soba shop serving dozuki soba, made from Yatsugatake foothills buckwheat without using a stone mill; open 11:00-15:00, closed Thursdays.

food.name: Shinshu Ajiyashiki Sasaoka
food.description: Restaurant serving Tateshina soba made with whole-grain highland buckwheat flour, and eel; open 11:00-14:30 and 17:00-20:00 (last order), closed Wednesdays and the 1st and 3rd Tuesdays.

food.name: Honteuchi Soba Choju Sarashina
food.name_ja: 本手打ちそば 長寿更科
food.description: Serves 100% buckwheat soba made with Yatsugatake-foothill buckwheat and no binder; open 11:00-14:30 and 17:00-19:30 (last order), closed Tuesdays.

food.name: Soba Dokoro Ryokuen
food.description: Soba restaurant on Daimon-kaido Pass facing Mt. Tateshina, operating for over 30 years; open 9:00-17:00, with irregular closing days.

food.name: Tateshina Soba Meruhen
food.name_ja: 蓼科そば メルヘン
food.description: Shinshu soba shop on Meruhen-kaido in the Tateshina central highlands; open 11:00-15:00, closed Wednesdays, from May to late November.

food.name: Teuchi Soba Mokubo
food.description: Handmade soba shop using Tateshina spring water and stone-milled Yatsugatake flour, made each morning; winter-only toji soba is eaten shabu-shabu style; open 11:00-15:00.

food.name: Sobasho Tateshina Kogen
food.name_ja: そば庄 蓼科高原店
food.description: Hand-cut soba shop in a relocated Tenpo-era waki-honjin from Shimosuwa on the old Nakasendo; open 11:00-15:00, closed Tuesdays.

food.name: Soba Dokoro Yamanami
food.description: Handmade soba shop using stone-milled local flour; all seats view Lake Tateshina and Yatsugatake; open 11:00-15:00 and 17:30-19:30 by reservation or until sold out, closed Wed (none in summer; Tue-Thu in winter).

food.name: Migotoya Honten
food.description: Soba shop serving slightly thick country-style soba, a wasabi-green zaru set with mushroom rice, and pesticide-free vegetable tempura from the owner's field; open 11:30-15:00, closed Wednesdays (daily in August).

food.name: Mingei Shokudokoro Danbee Soba Moegi no Ie
food.name_en: Mingei Shokudokoro Danbee Soba Moegi no Ie
food.name_ja: 民芸食事処 だんべえそば もえぎの家
food.description: Soba and udon shop serving self-foraged wild vegetables; Danbee set (soba or udon, three wild vegetables and tempura) is 1,890 yen, plus hoto, miso-nikomi udon, nabeyaki udon and siphon coffee, open 11:00-20:00 (last order 19:30).

food.name: FARMER'S TABLE
food.description: Restaurant in Tateshina; open 11:00-20:00 (last order 19:00), closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays.

food.name: Restaurant Mori
food.description: Restaurant on the Venus Line with a red triangular roof, serving 250g pork-loin shogayaki and Napolitan; lunch from 650 yen; open 11:00-14:00 and 17:00-21:00; closed Tuesdays.

food.name: Restaurant Domingo Chino
food.name_ja: レストラン ドミンゴ茅野店
food.description: Spanish-Mexican restaurant serving beef stew doria, cheese spaghetti, pasta, paella, shrimp ajillo and escargot, plus wine and cheese; open 11:00-14:30 and 17:00-21:30 (Sundays and holidays to 21:00); closed Mondays.

food.name: Sky City
food.description: Winter-only restaurant on the 2nd floor of the Kurumayama Plateau Visitor Center; meals 10:00-15:00 and cafe service 9:00-16:00 (last orders), closed Monday-Thursday except year-end and New Year.

food.name: Paul's Kitchen
food.description: Australian restaurant serving hamburgers, spare ribs and coffee; open 11:30-15:00 and 17:00-20:00, closed Thu and Fri, open daily in August and weekends only in winter except year-end and New Year.

food.name: Tommy's Style
food.description: Restaurant in a broadleaf forest using local highland vegetables and additive-free house-smoked foods; dinner by reservation; closed in winter; call for hours.

food.name: Shakunage
food.description: Restaurant serving seasonal Shinshu dishes with local ingredients, home-grown vegetables and wild plants, including yamaimo, carp, sakura-niku, basashi and soba-mai; lunch 11:30-14:00, dinner 17:00-22:00; closed Mondays.

food.name: Shihokuan
food.description: Folk-house cafe over 110 years old in Kitayama Serigasawa, serving handmade Suwa regional cuisine, with a gallery upstairs; open Thu-Sun 10:00-17:00, lunch 11:30-13:30 (16 meals); closed Mon-Wed.

food.name: Kappo Mori no Ie
food.description: Kappo restaurant a two-minute walk from Chino Station, using Shinshu ingredients and seasonal produce; open 11:30-23:00, closed Mondays, with private rooms for 2 to 100 guests.

food.name: Kappo Tamura
food.description: Japanese restaurant on the Venus Line serving kamameshi lunches, tebako and eel sets, and seasonal course dinners; open 11:00-14:00 and 17:00-22:00, closed Mondays (next day if a holiday).

food.name: Nihon Ryori Sakaecho
food.description: Japanese restaurant with Sakaecho bento and horse-sashimi bowls at lunch, omakase sets and local-chicken bowls at night, and steamed-then-grilled eel; open 11:00-14:00 and 17:00-21:00 (may change), closed Thursdays.

food.name: Mori no Ie Hanamaki
food.description: Serves dote-kusa dishes using wild plants from field ridges, plus traditional Shinshu dishes; lunch courses 1,200 and 1,700 yen, dinner course 2,500 yen; open 12:00-14:00 and 17:00-21:00; closed Mondays.

food.name: Gohan Dokoro Tateshina
food.name_ja: ごはん処 たてしな
food.description: Meal restaurant serving Showa-era home cooking with alcohol; open from 17:30; closed Tuesdays; reservation required.

food.name: Gozoku no Yakata Daitoen
food.description: Local-cuisine restaurant in a farmhouse more than 100 years old, serving wild-boar botan nabe; lunch is soba only; open 12:00-14:00 and 17:00-21:00 (last order 20:00).

food.name: Yamimian (Tateshina Ai)
food.description: Japanese restaurant serving mountain kaiseki with spring mountain greens, highland vegetables and autumn mushrooms, plus a lunch mini-kaiseki; open 11:30-14:30 and 18:00-21:00, no fixed closing day, reservation required.

food.name: Tateshina Kohan Tade no Hana
food.description: Lakeside Japanese restaurant serving kaiseki with seasonal Tateshina ingredients, charcoal-grilled dishes, house-smoked foods, and local sake, shochu and wine; open 11:30-14:00 and 18:00-21:30 by reservation.

food.name: Maruhei Kawazakana-ten
food.description: Freshwater fish and eel restaurant serving Lake Suwa fish and local dishes; meals 11:30-14:00, eel bento 11:30-18:00, shop sales 10:00-19:00, closed Wednesdays.

food.name: Kuretakezushi
food.description: Sushi restaurant serving Edomae sushi, local sake, tempura, grilled fish and set meals; open 11:00-23:00, closed Mondays.

food.name: Sushi Dokoro Mitsuyama
food.description: Sushi restaurant serving nigiri and barachirashi; open 11:00-13:30 and 17:00-21:30 (until 21:00 on Sundays), closed Mondays (next day if Monday is a holiday).

food.name: Cafe Tateshina Ice Cream
food.description: Sweets and bakery shop in Chino.

food.name: Bakery Restaurant Epi
food.name_ja: ベーカリーレストラン エピ
food.description: Sweets and bakery shop in Chino.

food.name: Dessert & Cafe Tatekkuru
food.description: Cake shop by Lake Tateshina serving seasonal-fruit cakes and parfaits with house-made gelato and compote; open 11:00-18:00 (last order 17:30), closed Tuesdays and the 2nd and 4th Wednesdays.

food.name: Shinshu Daikokuya Sweets & Cafe
food.description: Sweets cafe serving desserts, light meals and nel-drip Brazil Yoshimatsu coffee and tea; open 9:30-16:30 (last order 16:00), closed Mondays, Tuesdays and the 4th Wednesday.

food.name: Anniversary Tirol
food.name_ja: アニバーサリーチロル
food.description: Western confectionery shop founded in 1953, selling about 15 fresh sweets and 40 baked sweets, with a second-floor eat-in cafe. Open 9:30-19:00, closed Mondays.

food.name: Baigetsu Yonezawa-ten / Gelateria Shun
food.name_ja: 梅月米沢店・ジェラテリア旬
food.description: Japanese sweets and gelato shop; salt yokan is sold as a souvenir and seasonal gelato, including Japanese-style gelato, is served; open 9:00-17:00, closed Fridays in winter only.

sights.description: Azalea viewing spot in Chino.

sights.description: Daylily viewing spot in Chino.

sights.description: Cherry blossom viewing spot in Chino.

sights.description: Komakusa viewing spot in Chino.

sights.name_en: Chino City Sports Park in the urban center, a popular cherry-blossom picnic spot listed on Go NAGANO.

sights.name: Omi Village Butai Sakura
sights.name_en: Butai-zakura at former Zagoto Elementary Butai schoolhouse (built Meiji 7): a rare half-double weeping higan cherry about 350 years old.
sights.description: Cherry tree about 350 years old, a rare semi-double weeping red higan type whose petal count varies by bloom, before the Meiji 7 former Zakoji Elementary stage schoolhouse, lit at night.

sights.name: Toyama Sakura Kawazu Sakura
sights.name_en: Toyama-go cherry plantings: about 60-70 Somei-yoshino along 2.5 km of the Toyama River left bank, plus early Kawazu and weeping cherries on the right.
sights.description: Cherry blossom viewing spot in Iida.

sights.name: Ho Hisashi Tera no Shakunage (Shakunage)
sights.name_en: Hojuji Temple rhododendrons on a terrace overlooking the Tenryu River; bloom typically late April to mid-May.
sights.description: Rhododendrons in the natural garden of a Zen temple on a rise overlooking the Tenryu River, in season from late April to mid-May.

sights.name: no Soko Yama Forest Park
sights.name_en: Nosokoyama Forest Park with cherry blossoms in spring, maple color in autumn, playgrounds, and camping facilities.
sights.description: Forest park with cherry blossoms in spring, maple leaves in autumn, playground equipment, and camping facilities.

sights.name: Myo Kon Park
sights.name_en: Myokin Park for mallet golf, cycling, nearby amago fishing on the Matsukawa, camping, azaleas, and autumn color.
sights.description: Park with mallet golf, cycling, a campground, and amago fishing in the nearby Matsukawa, plus spring azaleas and autumn leaves.

sights.name: Mitsuishi no Shidarezakura
sights.name_en: Weeping cherry by the Sanseki stones on the old Akiba road in Shimohisakata; about 300 years old and 15 m tall.
sights.description: Weeping cherry, estimated 300 years old and 15 meters tall, planted beside the Mitsuishi rocks along the old Akiba road; nearby potholes are a prefectural natural monument.

sights.name: Sakuramaru no Fufu Sakura
sights.name_en: Meoto-zakura at former Iida Castle Sakuramaru: a weeping cherry and Edohigan said to be about 400 years old and roughly 20 m tall.
sights.description: Weeping cherry and Edohigan cherry trees bloom leaning together at the former Iida Castle Sakuramaru palace, about 20 m tall with trunks about 10 m in girth and an estimated age of 400 years.

sights.name: Kiyohide Sakura
sights.name_en: Seishu-zakura, an Edohigan at Atago Shrine traditionally planted in 1240; Iida oldest cherry and a city natural monument.
sights.description: Edohigan cherry at Atago Shrine, said to have been planted by Hoin Kiyohide in 1240, designated an Iida City natural monument and estimated over 760 years old, with night illumination.

sights.name: Omiya Tori no Sakura Namiki
sights.name_en: About 700 m of cherry trees (about 150, mainly Somei-yoshino) from Omiya Shrine toward Apple Avenue, with blossom festivals and night lighting.
sights.description: Cherry avenue of about 150 trees, mainly Somei-yoshino and higan cherry, running about 700 m from Omiya Shrine, with a blossom tunnel, festival, and night lighting when in bloom.

sights.name: Sen Sho Tera no Shidarezakura
sights.name_en: Weeping cherry over 400 years old in front of Senshoji main hall, with night lighting during bloom.
sights.description: A weeping cherry more than 400 years old stands in front of Senshoji Temple's main hall, with a gentle-faced Buddha statue beneath it and night illumination.

sights.name: Yasutomi Cherry Tree
sights.description: Prefectural natural monument Edohigan cherry at Iida City Art Museum, estimated 450 years old and 20 meters tall.

sights.name: Hinatsu Konosuke Memorial Museum
sights.description: Modeled on Iida-born writer Hinatsu Konosuke's later home, it displays his books, letters, and belongings.

sights.name: Iida City Archaeological Museum
sights.description: Displays pre-pottery artifacts from Chuo Expressway excavations and stands beside Kaizenji Temple.

sights.name: Iida City Kawamoto Kihachiro Puppet Art Museum
sights.description: Art museum of puppet artist Kawamoto Kihachiro, showing over 100 puppets from NHK dramas, animation, and commercials.

sights.name: Tenryukyo Autumn Foliage
sights.description: Where the Tenryu River is narrowest, Tenryukyo's autumn colors peak from early to mid-November.

sights.name: Kunio Yanagita Museum
sights.description: This relocated 1927 Tokyo study of folklore pioneer Kunio Yanagita displays his books and Iida connections.

sights.name: Shusui Beauty Painting Museum
sights.description: Active nihonga painter Shusui, pupil of the late Ito Tansui, permanently exhibits his beauty paintings.

sights.name: Kannon Reisui Spring
sights.description: This drinkable Ryuenji spring, long used as household water, is very high in calcium and magnesium.

sights.name: Ryuenji Temple
sights.description: Toyama clan graves lie beneath old cedars, and Kannon Reisui spring rises within the temple grounds.

sights.name: Yanagishima Checkpoint Site
sights.description: Toyama Tosa-no-kami built it on Ieyasu's orders to police Osaka fugitives and control timber.

sights.name: Former Zakouji Omi School Building
sights.description: Built as both kabuki stage and school, it is the prefecture's oldest school and draws spring blossom visitors.

sights.name: Imada Puppets
sights.description: Puppetry began in 1704 to enliven the Omiya Hachiman Shrine festival and is dedicated there each October.

sights.name: Kudagayu Ritual
sights.description: Held at Nakago Hachiman Shrine to divine that year's crop harvest.

sights.name: Na no Hana Park no Himawari
sights.name_en: Sunflowers planted at Nanohana Park in summer (peak around 10 August) in rotation with the spring rape blossoms.
sights.description: Sunflowers planted in summer at Na no Hana Park to prevent continuous cropping of rapeseed, usually starting around August 4, peaking around August 10, and cut after Obon.

sights.name: Na no Hana Park no Na no Hana
sights.name_en: Nanohana Park spring rape-blossom fields (late April-early May), a viewpoint over the Chikuma River toward the Sekita range.
sights.description: Canola park on a low hill east of the Chikuma River, motif of the song Oborozukiyo, viewing the river and snowy Sekita Mountains, about 15 minutes by car from Togari, Nozawa, and Maguse onsen.

sights.name: Hokuryu Mizumi no Na no Hana
sights.description: Rapeseed fields spread along the shore of Lake Hokuryu in spring, set against the blue lake and green mountains.

sights.name: Madarao Highlands no Ryukinka
sights.name_en: Marsh marigolds at Madarao Kogen Numahara wetland, typically blooming early to late May after the skunk cabbage.
sights.description: Ryukinka flowers at Numanohara Marsh on the Madarao Highlands, blooming after skunk cabbage as snow melts, usually viewed from early to late May.

sights.name: Madarao Highlands no Mizubasho
sights.description: Colony of Asian skunk cabbage at Numanohara wetland, seen as the snow melts, with a usual peak from late April to mid-May.

sights.name: Nishi Otaki Dam Cherry Blossoms
sights.name_en: Cherry trees at Nishi-Otaki Dam Sakura Plaza, with blossoms reflected on the reservoir in late April-early May.
sights.description: Cherry blossoms at Nishi-Otaki Dam are usually viewed from late April to early May, with Sakura Plaza in front of the dam and blossoms reflected on the water.

sights.name: Nagamine Supotsu Park Cherry Blossoms
sights.name_en: About 550 mountain cherries and Somei-yoshino around Hariko Pond at Nagamine Sports Park (late April-early May).
sights.description: Cherry trees, about 550 Oyama-zakura and Somei-yoshino, lining the pond and lawn, usually in bloom from late April to early May, some varieties until mid-May.

sights.name: Chikumagawa Sakurazutsumi
sights.name_en: About 700 cherry trees along roughly 4 km of the Chikuma River embankment, peaking mid- to late April with snowy hills beyond.
sights.description: Cherry avenue of about 700 trees along about 4 km of the Chikuma River beside Route 117, with Somei-yoshino and Oyama-zakura usually peaking from mid to late April.

sights.name: Iiyama Castle Park Cherry Blossoms
sights.name_en: Iiyama Castle ruins park with restored gates and walls; a major local cherry spot hosting an April castle sakura festival.
sights.description: A castle built by Uesugi Kenshin as a strategic base for the Shinano invasion has restored gates, earthworks, and stone walls, and an April cherry-blossom festival with lantern-lit night blossoms.

sights.name: Taka Gen In no Ajisai

sights.name: Nabekura Highlands

sights.name: Narazawa Great Tengu (Narazawa Shrine Festival)

sights.name: Lake Raisenji

sights.name: Peach Blossoms of Tankakyo

sights.name: Sanseiji Gorge

sights.description: Buses cover 22.8 kilometers of autumn foliage from Todai-guchi to Kitazawa Pass in about one hour.

sights.name: Atsuta Shrine

sights.name: Odo Mei

sights.name: Otona Gorge

sights.name: Giant Ceramic Mural

sights.name: Ikenotaira Tortoise-Shell Rock

sights.name: Tsukise Circling Drum

sights.name: Obuse Ranch milgreen

sights.name: Shakaifukushi Hojin Kuri no Mi Sono

sights.name: Shutsu So Park no Katakuri
sights.description: Dogtooth violet viewing spot in Okaya.

sights.name: Kosaka Kannon In (Kosaka Park) no Ajisai
sights.description: Hydrangea planting of 800 plants in full bloom in mid-July after the rainy season, in blue, white, and purple, with a view of Lake Suwa.

sights.name: Yokogawa Kawa no Sakura Achi
sights.description: Cherry-blossom arch of about 400 trees, mainly Somei-yoshino, extending about 4 km along both embankments of the Yokogawa River.

sights.name: Former Watanabe Family Residence
sights.description: Birthplace of Shinshu's first minister, Kunitake, and sons Chiaki and Chifuyu; called the origin of modern houses. Prefectural treasure.

sights.name: Ilf Children's Art Museum
sights.description: Features Takei Takeo, who coined doga, and permanent works by Maurice Sendak of Where the Wild Things Are.

sights.name: Toriidaira Yamabiko Park
sights.description: A vast, scenic, nature-rich park on a 1,000-meter rise overlooking Lake Suwa, Yatsugatake, and the Alps.

sights.name: Okaya Lakeside Park
sights.description: A Lake Suwa fountain rises 55 meters and is lit at night; cherry rows bloom fully in spring.

sights.name: Okaya Civic General Gymnasium
sights.description: A popular civic gymnasium for health promotion and a venue for various sports tournaments.

sights.name: Suwa Lakehill Country Club
sights.description: Its wooded course, rated 71.1, stirs challenge from average golfers to low-handicap players.

sights.name: Autumn Foliage at Izuhaya Park
sights.description: Peak late October to mid-November; many species yield shifting red, yellow, and orange leaves, also known for spring dogtooth violets.

sights.name: Takabocchi Plateau and Mount Hachibuse
sights.description: Refreshing plateau overlooking Lake Suwa, Yatsugatake, Mount Fuji, and the Alps; azaleas bloom in June, daylilies in July.

sights.name: Swans of Lake Suwa
sights.description: Swans, a winter symbol since two whooper swans in 1974, now exceed 200 yearly, viewable against Mount Fuji.

sights.name: Prefectural Izuhaya Park
sights.description: Shrine grove is a city natural monument; 240 species color autumn, and the maple festival lights the park at night.

sights.name: Enrei Onodachi Park Lookout
sights.description: Famous for autumn leaves and birdsong in Japan's 100 Soundscapes; the only view of Yatsugatake, Fuji, and the Northern Alps.

sights.name: Kosaka Kannon-in Temple
sights.description: Rebuilt in 1715 by fourth Takashima lord Tadataka; Okuma-style work by Ushiyama Zensuke and Hanaoka Isoemon.

sights.name: Nashikubo Ruins
sights.description: A typical mountain settlement ruin on an alluvial fan overlooking Mount Fuji, where Nashikubo-style pottery was found.

sights.name: Former Hayashi Family Residence
sights.description: Silk-reeling family's mansion from the industry's peak, with an adjoining tearoom and Western house wrapped in gold leather paper.

sights.name: Dehaya Park
sights.description: Vast dogtooth-violet colonies delight visitors in mid to late April, and autumn foliage in late October to early November.

sights.name: Enrei Goryotachi Park
sights.description: Panoramic views of Lake Suwa, Yatsugatake, Mount Fuji, and the Northern Alps; also known for sunrise and sunset.

sights.name: Okaya City Yamabiko International Skating Center
sights.description: A comprehensive sports facility where elite athletes train and beginners and the public can casually enjoy skating.

sights.name: Yamabiko Skate Forest Ice Arena
sights.description: Beside Yamabiko Park, families skate and curl even in summer on Japan's top-class ice, except mid-July through September.

sights.name: Enrei Outdoor Activity Center
sights.description: Adjacent to scenic Enrei Goryotachi Park, with a green sports house, campsite, lawn, field athletics, and running course.

sights.name: Wild Birds of Enrei Goryotachi Park
sights.description: Every Sunday in May and June a bird bus runs; the beautiful songs and scenery rank among Japan's 100 Soundscapes.

sights.name: Autumn Foliage at Enrei Goryotachi Park
sights.description: A nature park around Shiojiri Pass, designated a prefectural bird forest, offering birdsong and autumn foliage worth seeing.

sights.name: no Zokido Forest Park
sights.description: Forest park with Central Alps views, spring azaleas, blueberry picking from summer into autumn, a campground, and star viewing; open late April-late May and mid-July-late September.

sights.name: Suhara Yado no Mizu Fune
sights.description: Water troughs hollowed from sawara logs, used since the post-town era for washing rice, vegetables, and dishes and as a resting place.

sights.description: Shrine founded in 1344 with four national Important Cultural Property halls, Zao, Hakusan, Izu and Kumano, in plain one-bay nagare-zukuri, open only during festivals.

sights.name: Sadakatsu Tera

sights.name: Nozokido Forest Park Azalea Garden
sights.description: Colonies of three-leaf and mountain azaleas fill the park, purple in late April and red from early to mid-May.

sights.name: Weeping Cherries at Joshoji Temple

sights.name: Shinshu Famous and Secret Waters: Atera Gorge Beautiful Face Water

sights.name: Karahana Ken Marsh

sights.name: Naka Tsuna Koshu Hen no Asagimadara

sights.description: Poem monument to Kaneda Chizuru, born in 1902, who liked poetry from girlhood, belonged to the Araragi school, and died at 33.
